subject: Archive policy & SIG gap map — proposed MAP items and DPA retention clarifications

From: Asha Ramanathan <asha@finluma.com>

Cc: procurement@finluma.com, FinLuma Legal <legal@finluma.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP item: archival/retention + quick SIG question

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the kickoff earlier this week. As we build out the mutual action plan (MAP) for FinLuma's evaluation, Legal asked for a short write-up that clarifies two items before we finalize the timeline: 1) how Redwood proposes to handle long-term archival for debug / audit (retention windows, export formats, disposal), and 2) a small SIG/CAIQ gap list specifically around data export, key management, and DPA carve-outs.

Practically, they want a single page we can include in the MAP (to attach to the DPA) that states: retention tiers, who owns export responsibilities during a termination, and whether Redwood supports evidence export in an encrypted archive. Also — if you have a SOC 2 report and a prefilled SIG matrix we can review, please share.

We are aiming to close eval + procurement on or before Oct 22 so this will help Legal & Procurement size contract redlines.

Can you share a proposal by Friday 9/17? If you prefer, loop in your security lead and we can do a 20-min working call.

Thanks,
Asha

FinLuma

Subject: Re: MAP item: archival/retention + quick SIG question

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear ask.

High level response up front: yes, we can provide an archival/export path in encrypted archives and we will include a short retention table in the MAP. For DPA language we typically offer three retention tiers: 30 days (default transient logs), 12 months (standard product telemetry & analytics), and configurable archival (customer-controlled, typically 7 years for regulated customers). We’ll propose default values plus an annex with an export checklist (who triggers export, format, encryption).

On SIG/CAIQ: we maintain a prefilled SIG matrix for common fintech asks. My plan is to: 1) share our SOC 2 report (redacted where required), 2) attach a short SIG-gap matrix (callouts for KMS, escrow, and export traceability), and 3) add a proposed MAP line-item set that Legal can use to accept the retention annex and evidence transfer obligations.

Can Kimberly drop the SOC 2 and the draft SIG-gap matrix here by EOD? Jonas — can you confirm the proposed MAP milestone wording for acceptance criteria (SOC 2 evidence + DPA signed + export-runbook delivered)?

If that works, we’ll circulate a 1-page MAP appendix that FinLuma can attach to their DPA.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Manager — Redwood Inference

Thanks — proposed acceptance criteria below (short bullets we can drop into the MAP appendix):
- MAP Security Acceptance: Delivery of redacted SOC 2 report and SIG-gap-matrix signed off by FinLuma (or explicit DPA carve-outs accepted).
- Evidence Handoff: Redwood will provide an encrypted archive (AES-256) of evidence and a signed manifest. Export responsibility: Redwood will produce a downloadable encrypted archive; FinLuma must provide a destination and key-handling instructions if they require customer-controlled keys.
- Retention Defaults: 30d (transient), 12mo (operational analytics), archival configurable (default 7y, adjustable by contract).
- Closure Trigger: Acceptance occurs when DPA signed and export-runbook validated in a joint smoke test.

I’ll draft the MAP appendix language and drop it here by EOD.

— Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions Architecture — Redwood Inference
